claim_1.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assays analysis of plasma from 212 TIV-vaccinated subjects across the 2007–2011 influenza seasons showed that day 28 antibody responses decreased with increasing age compared to younger subjects.

sources.quote: In the 2010 and 2011 seasons, in which elderly subjects were included, antibody responses showed a significant decrease with age (Figures 1B, 1C, and S1C), consistent with previous studies (Seidman et al., 2012).

claim_2.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assays analysis of plasma from 212 TIV-vaccinated subjects across the 2007–2011 influenza seasons showed that vaccines from different seasons induced varying levels of day 28 antibody responses compared to each other.

sources.quote: Vaccines from different seasons induced varying levels of HAI responses, and there was a significant decrease in the response with age (Figure 1C).

claim_3.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assays analysis of plasma from TIV-vaccinated subjects with measurements at day 28 and day 180 showed that antibody responses peaked at day 28 and declined by day 180 compared to day 28.

sources.quote: The antibody responses peaked at day 28 (D28), with a significant decline in most subjects by D180 (Figure 6A).

claim_4.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assays analysis of plasma from subjects measured at day 28 and day 180 showed that day 180 antibody titers depended significantly on the original day 28 response compared to lower day 28 responses.

sources.quote: Because the D180 antibody titer shows significant dependence on the original antibody response generated on day 28 (Figure 6B), examining the molecular profile associated with the D180 response would identify many of the mechanisms responsible for generating the D28 response.

claim_5.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assays analysis of plasma from subjects measured at day 28 and day 180 showed that subjects with higher day 28 titers had a greater decrease in HAI response by day 180 compared to subjects with lower day 28 titers.

sources.quote: We observed that subjects with a higher D28 titer had a greater decrease in HAI response between D28 and D180, indicating increased difficulty to maintain higher levels of antibodies.

claim_6.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from TIV-vaccinated subjects across multiple influenza seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that interferon- and dendritic-cell-related blood transcription modules were enriched on days 1 and 3 after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0) in subjects with higher day 28 antibody responses.

sources.quote: BTMs related to the induction of interferons as well as the activation of dendritic cells (Figures 2A and 2B) were enriched on days 1 and 3 after TIV vaccination, whereas modules related to T cells at these time points were negatively associated with the antibody response.

claim_7.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from TIV-vaccinated subjects across multiple influenza seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that T-cell-related modules on days 1 and 3 after vaccination were negatively associated with day 28 antibody responses compared to subjects with higher antibody responses.

sources.quote: BTMs related to the induction of interferons as well as the activation of dendritic cells (Figures 2A and 2B) were enriched on days 1 and 3 after TIV vaccination, whereas modules related to T cells at these time points were negatively associated with the antibody response.

claim_8.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from TIV-vaccinated subjects across multiple influenza seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed robust enrichment of antibody-secreting-cell and cell-cycle-related modules on day 7 after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0) in subjects with higher day 28 antibody responses.

sources.quote: On day 7, there was a robust enrichment of ASC and cell cycle-related modules, consistent with our original study (Nakaya et al., 2011).

claim_9.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly TIV vaccinees across multiple seasons, using single-sample GSEA (ssGSEA) and an artificial neural network classifier, showed that module-level signatures predicted day 28 HAI responses in both young and elderly subjects compared to non-predictive baseline classification.

sources.quote: With this approach, we identified BTMs that predicted HAI responses in both the young and elderly groups with accuracies ranging between 79.0% and 80.2% and between 64.7% and 72.3%, respectively, using both day 3 and day 7 signatures (Figure 2C).

claim_10.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly TIV vaccinees showed that predictive molecular signatures of high day 28 HAI response were similar in elderly and young subjects compared to each other, despite lower antibody responses in the elderly.

sources.quote: This suggests that although the elderly had lower antibody responses to vaccination, the molecular signatures that were predictive of high HAI response remained the same.

claim_11.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from combined multi-season TIV studies, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that higher baseline B-cell- and T-cell-related module expression was positively correlated with increased day 28 antibody responses compared to lower baseline expression.

sources.quote: This approach revealed several B-cell- and T-cell-related modules whose expression pre-vaccination was positively correlated with an increased antibody response to vaccination in all studies (Figure 3A).

claim_12.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from combined multi-season TIV studies, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that higher baseline monocyte-related module expression was negatively correlated with day 28 antibody responses compared to lower baseline monocyte-module expression.

sources.quote: In contrast, modules related to monocytes were negatively correlated with antibody responses (Figures 3B–3G).

claim_13.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly subjects in the 2010 TIV season showed that the largest age-related difference in vaccine-induced gene expression occurred on day 1 after vaccination compared to later time points, with young subjects exhibiting many more upregulated and downregulated genes than elderly subjects.

sources.quote: By far the largest difference in overall expression between the two groups occurred on day 1, where the young exhibited a much greater number of both up- and downregulated genes.

claim_14.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly subjects in the 2010 TIV season, using weighted correlation network analysis (WGCNA), showed that interferon-related genes had similar temporal profiles but higher expression magnitude in young subjects compared to elderly subjects after vaccination.

sources.quote: Although the genes shared by clusters from young and elderly vaccinated individuals had similar temporal expression profiles, the magnitude of the expression of interferon-related genes differed, being higher in young individuals (Figure 4C).

claim_15.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from the 2010 and 2011 TIV seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that NK-cell-related modules increased with age on days 3 and 7 after vaccination compared to younger subjects.

sources.quote: Natural killer (NK) cell-related modules showed increased expression with age on both day 3 and day 7 after vaccination, and several monocyte modules showed increased expression with age on day 7.

claim_16.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from the 2010 and 2011 TIV seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that monocyte-related modules increased with age on day 7 after vaccination compared to younger subjects.

sources.quote: Natural killer (NK) cell-related modules showed increased expression with age on both day 3 and day 7 after vaccination, and several monocyte modules showed increased expression with age on day 7.

claim_17.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from the 2010 and 2011 TIV seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that B-cell-related modules decreased with age on days 3 and 7 after vaccination compared to younger subjects.

sources.quote: In contrast, many B cell modules showed decreased expression in older subjects on both day 3 and day 7.

claim_18.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from the 2010 and 2011 TIV seasons showed that B-cell modules M47.0 and M69 were enriched in younger subjects and in subjects with high antibody responses compared to elderly subjects and low responders.

sources.quote: Two B cell modules, M47.0 and M69, showed increased expression in younger subjects and in subjects with high antibody responses, whereas three monocyte- and myeloid-cell-related modules, S4, M4.3, and M11.0, were enriched in the elderly and were also associated with a decreased antibody response in the 2010 and 2011 seasons.

claim_19.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from the 2010 and 2011 TIV seasons showed that monocyte- and myeloid-cell-related modules S4, M4.3, and M11.0 were enriched in elderly subjects and associated with decreased antibody responses compared to younger subjects and high responders.

sources.quote: Two B cell modules, M47.0 and M69, showed increased expression in younger subjects and in subjects with high antibody responses, whereas three monocyte- and myeloid-cell-related modules, S4, M4.3, and M11.0, were enriched in the elderly and were also associated with a decreased antibody response in the 2010 and 2011 seasons.

claim_20.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from subjects with day 28 and day 180 follow-up, using correlation analysis, showed that plasmablast module S3 was positively associated with day 180 antibody response compared to lower plasmablast-module activity.

sources.quote: As expected, correlation analysis of plasmablast module BTM S3 shows a positive association with the D180 antibody response due to the effect of D28 antibody responses, generated through plasmablast expansion (Figure 6C).

claim_21.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from subjects with day 28 and day 180 follow-up, using correlation analysis, showed that plasmablast module S3 was not associated with the adjusted day 180/day 28 persistence residual compared to subjects with more persistent responses.

sources.quote: However, when we performed correlation between the plasmablast module activity and the D180/D28 residual, we no longer saw an association with the plasmablast expression (Figure 6D).

claim_22.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from subjects with day 28 and day 180 follow-up, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that cell movement- and adhesion-related modules including BTM 51 were enriched on days 3 and 7 in subjects with more persistent antibody responses compared to subjects with waning responses.

sources.quote: Among the BTMs most enriched in subjects with a persistent response on both days 3 and 7 were several modules associated with cell movement and adhesion, such as BTM 51 (Figure 6E).

claim_23.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from subjects with day 28 and day 180 follow-up, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that day 7 T-cell-related modules were negatively associated with the day 180/day 28 persistence residual compared to subjects with more persistent antibody responses.

sources.quote: In addition, the day 7 expression of a number of T-cell-related modules was negatively associated with the D180/D28 residual, indicating that increased T cell responses might potentially result in more transient antibody responses (Figure 6F).

claim_24.claim: Flow Cytometry Analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees at days 0–14 showed that total NK-cell proportions were higher in elderly subjects than in young subjects at baseline (day 0) and at all measured post-vaccination time points compared to young subjects.

sources.quote: Our analysis showed that proportions of total NK cells in elderly subjects were higher than those of young subjects at baseline as well as at all the time points studied (days 0–14).

claim_25.claim: Flow Cytometry Analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees at days 0–14 showed that vaccination increased the percentage of NK cells in elderly subjects compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Of note, vaccination induced an increase in the percentage of NK cells in the elderly subjects; in contrast, in the young there was a reduction in the percentage of NK cells on day 1 after vaccination (Figure 5A).

claim_26.claim: Flow Cytometry Analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees at days 0–14 showed that young subjects had a reduction in NK-cell percentage on day 1 after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Of note, vaccination induced an increase in the percentage of NK cells in the elderly subjects; in contrast, in the young there was a reduction in the percentage of NK cells on day 1 after vaccination (Figure 5A).

claim_27.claim: Flow Cytometry Analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees showed that elderly subjects had a higher frequency of CD56dimCD16++ NK cells and a lower frequency of CD56++ NK cells at baseline (day 0) compared to young subjects.

sources.quote: We observed a higher frequency of CD56dimCD16++ cells coincident with a lower frequency of CD56++ cells in the elderly at baseline, consistent with previous studies (Figure 5C; Solana et al., 2014).

claim_28.claim: Flow Cytometry Analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees showed that CD56dimCD16++ NK cells increased in elderly subjects on day 1 after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: The distribution of these subpopulations was relatively stable during the response, with CD56dimCD16++ cells showing a small but significant increase in the elderly on day 1 after vaccination and CD56++ cells increasing in the young on day 7.

claim_29.claim: Flow Cytometry Analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees showed that CD56++ NK cells increased in young subjects on day 7 after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: The distribution of these subpopulations was relatively stable during the response, with CD56dimCD16++ cells showing a small but significant increase in the elderly on day 1 after vaccination and CD56++ cells increasing in the young on day 7.

claim_30.claim: Flow Cytometry Analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees showed that all three NK-cell subsets in elderly subjects had increasing CD69 activation after vaccination, with highest expression on day 3 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Elderly subjects showed increasing activation after vaccination in all three subsets, with highest expression on day 3.

claim_31.claim: Flow Cytometry Analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees showed that young subjects exhibited CD69 activation of the CD56dimCD16++ NK subset only on day 1 and at a lower level than elderly subjects compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: In contrast, the young exhibited activation of the CD56dimCD16++ subset as measured by CD69 expression only on day 1 and at a lower level than in the elderly.

claim_32.claim: Flow Cytometry Analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees showed that monocyte proportions were higher in elderly subjects than in young subjects at baseline (day 0) and throughout the study compared to young subjects.

sources.quote: In addition to NK cells, we also observed higher proportions of monocytes among the elderly at baseline and during the entire duration of the study compared to young subjects (Figure S6A).

claim_33.claim: Flow Cytometry Analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees showed that total monocyte percentages increased substantially on day 1 after vaccination in both young and elderly subjects compared to baseline (day 0), then returned to or below baseline.

sources.quote: In both groups, the percentage of total monocytes in PBMCs increased substantially on day 1 after vaccination, then returned to or below baseline levels.

claim_34.claim: Flow Cytometry Analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees showed that elderly subjects had a slight increase in intermediate monocytes compared to young subjects.

sources.quote: The distribution of monocyte subsets was similar in both groups, with the elderly having a slight increase in intermediate monocytes compared to young (Figure S6C).

claim_35.claim: Flow Cytometry Analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees showed that CCR5 expression in classical and intermediate monocytes peaked on day 1 after vaccination in both young and elderly subjects compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: In both the young and elderly, CCR5 expression peaked in classical and intermediate monocytes on day 1 after vaccination, corresponding with the inflammation associated with the innate immune response.

claim_36.claim: Flow Cytometry Analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees showed that elderly subjects had increased CCR5 expression in classical and intermediate monocytes compared to young subjects.

sources.quote: Elderly subjects showed increased CCR5 expression in classical and intermediate monocytes compared to the young, whereas young subjects had higher CD86 expression in these subsets.

claim_37.claim: Flow Cytometry Analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees showed that young subjects had higher CD86 expression in classical and intermediate monocytes compared to elderly subjects.

sources.quote: Elderly subjects showed increased CCR5 expression in classical and intermediate monocytes compared to the young, whereas young subjects had higher CD86 expression in these subsets.

claim_38.claim: miRNA expression profiling of PBMCs from a subset of young and elderly subjects in the 2010 TIV season at days 1, 3, and 7 showed significantly different post-vaccination miRNA profiles in elderly subjects compared to young subjects.

sources.quote: We saw a significant difference in the miRNA profiles between these two groups.

claim_39.claim: miRNA expression profiling of PBMCs from a subset of young and elderly subjects in the 2010 TIV season at days 1, 3, and 7 showed that most differentially expressed miRNAs in elderly subjects were upregulated after vaccination, particularly on days 1 and 7, compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Whereas a majority of the differentially expressed miRNA in the elderly were upregulated after vaccination, particularly on days 1 and 7, the young exhibited predominantly downregulation of miRNA.

claim_40.claim: miRNA expression profiling of PBMCs from a subset of young and elderly subjects in the 2010 TIV season at days 1, 3, and 7 showed that young subjects exhibited predominantly downregulation of miRNAs after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Whereas a majority of the differentially expressed miRNA in the elderly were upregulated after vaccination, particularly on days 1 and 7, the young exhibited predominantly downregulation of miRNA.

claim_41.claim: miRNA expression profiling of PBMCs from a subset of young and elderly subjects in the 2010 TIV season showed that elderly subjects had a larger number of miRNAs negatively correlated with day 28 antibody response compared to young subjects.

sources.quote: We again saw differences between the young and elderly subjects, with the elderly having a larger number of miRNA negatively correlating with the antibody response when compared with the young.

claim_42.claim: miRNA expression profiling of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees, using single-sample GSEA (ssGSEA) integration with transcriptomic data, showed coordinated groups of blood transcription modules on day 1 after vaccination that were correlated with several miRNAs compared to modules without such correlations.

sources.quote: We then performed correlation analysis between all miRNA-BTM pairs, revealing groups of modules that appear to be regulated together by several miRNA (Figure 7D) on day 1 after vaccination.

claim_43.claim: miRNA expression profiling of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees, using TargetScan integration with transcriptomic data, showed that the antiviral interferon signature module M75 on day 1 after vaccination had potential novel miRNA regulators including miR-424 compared to genes in the module without predicted miRNA targeting.

sources.quote: This miRNA-mRNA network suggests potential novel regulators of the interferon response after vaccination, such as miR-424.

claim_44.claim: miRNA expression profiling of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees, using TargetScan integration with transcriptomic data, showed that miR-424 was predicted to target OAS3 and CXCL10 in the antiviral interferon response network compared to genes not identified as miR-424 targets.

sources.quote: This miRNA was predicted to target OAS3, a 2′–5′-oligoadenylate synthase involved in viral RNA degradation (Samuel, 2001), as well as CXCL10, an important chemokine induced by IFN-γ that serves as a chemoattractant for lymphocytes (Dufour et al., 2002).
